items.q: Why choose a fiberglass pool over concrete or vinyl liner?
items.a: Fiberglass is the fastest of the three to install, needs the least upkeep and rarely carries a big future repair bill, which is why many Jacksonville families choose it. The one-piece shell is made in a factory and set in weeks rather than months. Its smooth, non-porous gelcoat gives algae less to grip, so it typically needs fewer chemicals and less brushing. Concrete is the better answer when you need a truly custom shape, and vinyl usually has the lowest upfront price. See the full comparison guide.

items.q: How long does a fiberglass pool last?
items.a: A fiberglass pool shell is built to last for decades, and Barrier Reef backs its shells with a Lifetime Limited Structural Warranty, transferable once. Equipment such as pumps and heaters wears out sooner and is replaced separately. The 15-year finish warranty covers the gelcoat against blistering.

items.q: Is a fiberglass pool rough or slippery?
items.a: A fiberglass pool has a smooth gelcoat surface that feels comfortable on feet and swimsuits, unlike textured plaster or pebble. Barrier Reef molds texture into entry steps for grip. It's a common reason families with young children choose fiberglass.

items.q: What pool types and materials do you work with?
items.a: Fiberglass and concrete/gunite, plus paver decks, water features and outdoor kitchens. All built to take Florida sun, rain and daily use without looking tired in five years.

items.q: How much does a fiberglass pool cost in Jacksonville, compared with concrete and vinyl liner?
items.a: A typical installed fiberglass pool runs about $58,000–$85,000, compared with about $78,000–$110,000 for concrete and about $40,000–$65,000 for vinyl liner. These are published ranges, before deck, enclosure and fencing, and they vary with size, site and features. iTop Pools gives you a firm written price after the site visit. Build your own estimate to see how the pieces add up.

items.q: What is the total cost including deck, screen enclosure and fencing?
items.a: Your total depends mostly on deck size and material, whether you add a screen enclosure, and how much access your yard allows. Florida also requires a pool safety feature, which is included in iTop's permitting plan. Because each yard differs, we measure first and then give you one written price covering the pool, deck, enclosure and permits. The estimator shows which choices move the number most.

items.q: Why are your prices better than other builders I've quoted?
items.a: Because we don't subcontract. Most builders hire out the shell, the deck and the pavers, and each layer adds its own markup. We have our own specialized crew for all of it, so you pay for the work instead of the middlemen.

items.q: What should a complete pool quote include?
items.a: A complete fiberglass pool quote should cover the shell, delivery, excavation and haul-off, set and leveling, plumbing and equipment, backfill, coping, deck, electrical bonding, permits, Florida's required safety feature and start-up. If a bid leaves items out, it isn't cheaper, it's incomplete. See the full breakdown.

items.q: Which pool type costs least to own over 25 years?
items.a: Fiberglass usually has the lowest long-term ownership cost, because it avoids the two largest recurring bills: concrete resurfacing and vinyl liner replacement. Vinyl liners commonly need replacing every 10–15 years at about $3,000–$7,500 each, and Florida's sun can shorten that. Concrete needs periodic resurfacing and generally more chemicals. Actual costs depend on the pool and how it is cared for.

items.q: When is concrete a better choice than fiberglass?
items.a: Concrete is the better choice when you want a vanishing edge, an unusual size or a shape no mold offers. Expect a longer build and periodic resurfacing over the pool's life. If your yard truly needs something custom, iTop will tell you so.

items.q: Is vinyl cheaper than fiberglass?
items.a: Vinyl usually costs less upfront: Barrier Reef puts fiberglass at roughly 15–20% more than vinyl. But vinyl liners wear out and commonly need replacing every 10–15 years at about $3,000–$7,500 each, so the gap narrows over time. Compare both over the years you plan to own the pool.

items.q: How many fiberglass pool models does iTop offer?
items.a: iTop Pools offers all 22 Barrier Reef Pools USA models, covering rectangular, freeform, kidney, Roman and plunge shapes, from 16'6" to 40' long. Many come in several sizes. See them all on the pool models page.

items.q: What are the largest and smallest Barrier Reef pools?
items.a: The largest and deepest listed is the Whitsunday 40 Deep, at 40' by 15'8", 8'6" deep and about 28,350 gallons. The smallest are the Crispin and Pixie plunge pools, at 16'6" by 10' and about 3,100 gallons. See the plunge pools.

items.q: Can I fit a fiberglass pool in a small yard?
items.a: Yes, many small Northeast Florida yards can fit a fiberglass pool. Plunge models start at 16'6" by 10', and the narrow Coral Cay and Oasis suit long, slim lots. iTop Pools measures your yard on a free visit and tells you which shells clear your setbacks. Read our sizing guide.

items.q: Can I get a tanning ledge, spa, heater or salt system?
items.a: Yes, iTop Pools can build a tanning ledge, spa, heater or salt system into your project. Several Barrier Reef shells already have a built-in lounging ledge or integrated spa, and separate spas, sundecks and tanning ledges can be added to many models. Heat pumps, salt systems, LED lighting and automation are also available. Filter the pool models by feature to see which shells include them.

items.q: How long does a pool take, start to finish?
items.a: Once permits and HOA approvals are finalized, Barrier Reef puts a typical fiberglass install at 2–6 weeks, depending on size, site and weather. Our crew isn't split across other companies' jobs, which is why we can move faster than most. You'll get a firm timeline before we break ground.

items.q: Do I need permits, and will you handle them?
items.a: Yes, and yes. HOA approvals, engineering and county permitting are all ours to chase, including the safety feature Florida law requires. You don't fill out a form or make a phone call.

items.q: Who is actually on my property during the build?
items.a: Our own crew: the same specialized team on every iTop job, for both pools and pavers. No rotating subcontractors, no one you haven't met and no finger-pointing when something needs fixing.

items.q: Will weather push my timeline?
items.a: Heavy rain can move a day here and there. We tell you when it happens instead of going quiet, and we keep the schedule moving around it.

items.q: Will you need a crane to install my pool?
items.a: Sometimes. A fiberglass shell arrives in one piece, so pools behind the house, narrow lots or screened areas may need a crane to lift it over. If there's a clear, wide path, we can usually set it from the side. iTop Pools checks this on the site visit and includes it in your quote. Read the site access guide.

items.q: Is fiberglass good for Florida's soil, high water table and hurricanes?
items.a: Yes, a fiberglass pool suits Northeast Florida when it is installed for the site's soil and groundwater. iTop Pools in Jacksonville checks access and soil on the site visit and plans the set around local conditions. One rule matters above all: never drain a fiberglass pool yourself, because high groundwater after heavy rain can push an empty shell upward. Before a storm, leave the pool full and follow the Pool School storm guidance.

items.q: What pool safety rules apply in Florida?
items.a: Florida's Residential Swimming Pool Safety Act (Chapter 515, Florida Statutes) requires a new residential pool to have at least one approved safety feature, such as a compliant barrier, an approved safety cover, exit alarms or self-closing, self-latching doors. iTop Pools builds this into your quote. Read the permits guide.

items.q: Should I drain my pool before a hurricane?
items.a: No. Don't drain a fiberglass pool before a hurricane, because high groundwater after heavy rain can push an empty shell upward. Leave it full, turn off equipment power and secure loose items. Read our hurricane prep guide.

items.q: Do I need a screen enclosure in Northeast Florida?
items.a: You don't have to have a screen enclosure, but they're common in Northeast Florida because they keep out leaves and insects. They add a significant cost and slightly soften the water color. Try it both ways in the 3D studio, or read our enclosure guide.

items.q: How long is the swim season in Jacksonville without a heater?
items.a: Northeast Florida's mild climate gives a long swim season, but winter water gets cool without heating. A heat pump is the usual way to stretch the season, since Florida's mild winters suit them well. Tell iTop Pools how you'll use the pool, and we'll advise you.

items.q: How much maintenance does a fiberglass pool need?
items.a: A fiberglass pool needs less routine care than concrete or vinyl: mostly skimming, keeping the water balanced and standard equipment servicing. We build for low upkeep, and we walk you through exactly how to run it before we hand it over. Keep the water chemistry in range, because the finish warranty assumes it. Pool School has seasonal care guides written for Northeast Florida.

items.q: Will my pool be a lot of work to maintain?
items.a: We build for low upkeep. Routine cleaning and standard servicing are all it takes, and we walk you through exactly how to run it before we hand it over.

items.q: Do you offer energy-efficient options?
items.a: Yes. Options like salt systems, variable-speed pumps and automation can cut running costs. We'll tell you which ones actually pay for themselves in your setup.

items.q: Is saltwater better than chlorine for a fiberglass pool?
items.a: Either can work in a fiberglass pool. A salt system makes chlorine from salt in the water, so you handle less chlorine and many owners find the water softer, but you still test and balance it. Compare them.

items.q: What water chemistry levels should I keep?
items.a: Typical targets are pH of about 7.4–7.6, free chlorine of about 1–3 ppm and total alkalinity of about 80–120 ppm. Your handover sheet lists the exact targets for your pool and equipment. See your first 30 days.

items.q: What does the Barrier Reef warranty cover?
items.a: Barrier Reef provides a Lifetime Limited Structural Warranty on the shell, transferable once, plus a 15-year finish warranty against blistering. iTop separately warrants our installation work, and pumps, heaters and automation carry their own manufacturers' warranties. The written warranty documents govern. See who covers what.

items.q: Does the Barrier Reef warranty transfer if I sell my home?
items.a: Yes, once. Barrier Reef's Lifetime Limited Structural Warranty is one-time transferable to a subsequent purchaser. Keep your warranty paperwork and serial number, and read the full written warranty for its conditions.

items.q: How do I keep my pool warranty valid?
items.a: Keep your water balanced, don't drain the pool without calling first, and keep your paperwork. Finish warranties assume water chemistry stays in range. Barrier Reef's warranty covers the pool shell only, so the written document governs. See who covers what.

items.q: Do you offer financing?
items.a: Most homeowners finance at least part of a pool, usually through an unsecured pool loan, a home equity loan, a HELOC or a cash-out refinance. Rates and terms depend on the lender and your credit, so talk to iTop about your options when we go through your price. Our financing guide compares all four in plain English.

items.q: What is the monthly payment on a pool?
items.a: As an example only, a $65,000 project financed for 15 years at 7.99% APR is about $621 a month. Your payment depends on your lender, rate, term and down payment. Try the calculator.

items.q: What does the free consultation actually include?
items.a: A site visit, real measurements and a 3D design of your backyard, at no cost and with no obligation. You see exactly what you're buying before you commit a dollar. Book your free visit.

items.q: I'm not sure what I want. Can you help me decide?
items.a: That's what the 3D design is for. We lay out size, shape, decking and finishes based on your yard and your budget, and you change anything you want while it's still free to change.

items.q: Can I see a pool you already built?
items.a: Yes. Browse our work, or ask us and we'll arrange a visit to a finished project near you. We'd rather you stand next to the real thing.

items.q: What areas does iTop Pools serve?
items.a: iTop Pools builds across Northeast Florida, including Jacksonville, Ponte Vedra Beach, Nocatee, St. Johns, St. Augustine, Julington Creek, Fleming Island, Orange Park, Mandarin, Jacksonville Beach, Green Cove Springs and Middleburg. See our service areas.
